--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.set_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Set attribute values for one or more nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.set_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Set attribute values for one or more nodes. title: >- [Graph.set_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Set attribute values for one or more nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Set attribute values for one or more nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L32684-L32859){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.set_node_attrs( node_attr, values, nodes=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Set node attributes](../assets/graphs/set-node-attrs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Every node of a six-node graph carries a value x in a badge (A 3, B 5, C 2, D 4, E 6, F 1). The call names nodes B and F, outlined in the accent color; after it both read 7, while the other four nodes keep their values." width="100%"} Writes a single named attribute onto nodes, modifying the graph in place. The same value can be broadcast to many nodes, or different values can be supplied per node via a list (paired by position) or a dict (keyed by node). The attribute is created if it doesn't exist and overwritten if it does; all other attributes are left alone. This is the main way to attach data to nodes after they have been created, for example: - storing externally computed scores or classifications (e.g., from a model or a CSV) - tagging a known set of nodes with a category or flag - setting visual attributes such as `color` or `size` before plotting The `values=` dict form pairs naturally with methods that return `{node_id: value}` dictionaries (such as the `return_dict=True` mode of centrality measures). To set attributes on the current selection instead of on an explicit list, see `set_node_attrs_ws()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the attribute to set (e.g., `"color"`, `"score"`). This becomes a column of the same name in `get_node_df()`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any | list[Any] | dict[int, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The value(s) to write. Three forms are accepted: - a **dict** mapping node IDs or labels to values. Only nodes that appear both in the dict and in `nodes=` (all nodes, by default) are updated; nodes missing from the dict are left unchanged. - a **list** of values paired by position with `nodes=`. The list length must equal the number of target nodes. When `nodes=` is `None` the pairing follows the internal order of `get_node_ids()`, which is not necessarily insertion order, so pass `nodes=` explicitly when using a list. - **any other value** (a string, number, tuple, `None`, etc.), which is written to every target node. [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The nodes to update, given as node IDs (`int`) or labels (`str`), which may be mixed. If `None` (the default), all nodes in the graph are targeted. Labels are resolved to IDs, and an unknown label raises a `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `values=` is a list whose length doesn't match the number of target nodes, or if a label given in `nodes=` (or as a dict key) does not exist in the graph. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_node_attrs`) : Read one attribute back, as a dictionary keyed by node ID. [](`~set_node_attrs_ws`) : Set an attribute on the nodes in the current selection. [](`~set_edge_attrs`) : The same for edges. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A single value goes to every node listed in `nodes=`, or to every node if `nodes=` is left out. "C" isn't listed, so it gets no `flag`: ::: {#213a16ba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) graph.set_node_attrs("flag", True, nodes=["A", "B"]) graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Nodes it leaves out keep what they had: ::: {#178c1429 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.set_node_attrs("score", 0) graph.set_node_attrs("score", {"A": 60, "C": 75}) graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Ties across the split, member by member Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33), and the `faction` attribute records which side each member joined. Polars can find the ties that cross the split by joining each end of each edge to its faction: ::: {#34c57312 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ec.karate_club() sides = karate.get_node_df().select("label", "faction") source_sides = sides.rename({"label": "source", "faction": "from"}) target_sides = sides.rename({"label": "target", "faction": "to"}) crossing = ( karate.get_edge_df(labels=True) .join(source_sides, on="source") .join(target_sides, on="target") .filter(pl.col("from") != pl.col("to")) ) ends = pl.concat([crossing["source"], crossing["target"]]) per_member = ends.value_counts() ``` ::: To bring the counts back to the graph, `set_node_attrs()` first gives everyone 0, then a dictionary overwrites the members who have crossing ties. Member 2 has 5 of the 10: ::: {#2f23b4e3 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.set_node_attrs("crossing", 0) karate.set_node_attrs("crossing", dict(per_member.iter_rows())) crossers = karate.get_node_df().filter(pl.col("crossing") > 0) crossers.sort("crossing", descending=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
